Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a well-circumscribed cystic lesion in the right lower lobe traversed by a distinct band-like opacity (indicated by arrows), which is characteristic of a pulmonary vein crossing an intrapulmonary cyst. This anatomical relationship is clinically significant because interventions involving the cyst carry a risk of injuring the vessel and causing a systemic air embolism.
